question.text: If $z$ is a complex number such that $z^{2}=(\bar{z})^{2}$, then

options.text: either $z$ is purely real or purely imaginary

solution.text:
Let $z=x+i y$, then its conjugate $\bar{z}=x-i y$

Given that $z^{2}=(\bar{z})^{2}$

$\begin{array}{l}

\Rightarrow x^{2}-y^{2}+2 i x y=x^{2}-y^{2}-2 i x y \\

\Rightarrow 4 i x y=0

\end{array}$
